# `fonts/` — self-hosted woff2 payload

**Generated by** `tools/subset-fonts.sh` · **Captured** 2026-07-26 · **Do not hand-edit the `.woff2` files.**

This directory is the complete, self-hosted type payload for the site. No page may load
`fonts.googleapis.com` or `fonts.gstatic.com` at runtime — both origins are gone.

---

## 1. ⚠️ Read this first if you are T01 (`css/base.css`)

Three things in the source specs are **wrong or stale**, and copying them verbatim will break the site.

### 1.1 There are **18** files, not 6

`BRIEF.md` §2 and `reports/design-style.md` §3.4 both assume `pyftsubset` merged
`latin + latin-ext + vietnamese` into one file per face, giving 6 files named `*-vn.woff2`.

`pyftsubset` is not installed (see `IMPLEMENTATION-CONTRACT.md` Override 3), so we self-host
Google's own already-subsetted slices instead. Google ships **one file per subset**, so the real
payload is **6 faces × 3 subsets = 18 files**, and `css/base.css` needs **18 `@font-face` blocks**.

There is no file called `anton-400-vn.woff2`. It does not exist. Use the names in §2.

This is not a downgrade. Because each block carries its own `unicode-range`, the browser
downloads only the slices a page's actual characters need — a reader who never hits a
`latin-ext` codepoint never pays the 248 KB those six files cost.

### 1.2 The spec's `url('/fonts/…')` is a **sitewide 404**

`reports/design-style.md` §3.4 shows:

```css
/* ☠️ DO NOT COPY — root-absolute path */
@font-face { font-family:'Anton'; src:url('/fonts/anton-400-vn.woff2') format('woff2'); }
```

The site is a GitHub Pages **project page** served from `https://thepkz.github.io/minthep-portfolio/`.
`/fonts/…` resolves to `https://thepkz.github.io/fonts/…` → **404**, on every page, for every font.

`url()` in CSS resolves **relative to the stylesheet**, not the document. From `css/base.css`
the correct prefix is therefore `../fonts/`. Ready-to-paste blocks are in §4 — use those.

### 1.3 Be Vietnam Pro has no variable version

`wght@100..900` returns HTTP 400 for this family. Only static 400 / 500 / 700 exist and only
those three are shipped. **Never** let CSS ask for 600 — it triggers synthetic bolding, which
smears stacked Vietnamese diacritics.

**Total on disk: 716,660 bytes (699.9 KiB) across 18 files.**

That total is *not* what any visitor downloads. Realistic per-surface cost, counting only
`latin` + `vietnamese` (a Vietnamese page essentially never touches `latin-ext`):

| Surface | Faces used | Files fetched | Bytes |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| **A** — landing | anton-400, bvp-400/500/700, newsreader-vf | 10 | 287,924 (281 KiB) |
| **B** — articles | all six | 12 | 462,700 (452 KiB) |
| **C** — `wy/` | anton-400, bvp-400/500 | 6 | 94,056 (92 KiB) |

The six `latin-ext` files (253,960 bytes) are declared but, in practice, never requested.

### Verification state

All 18 files were checked at generation time:

- **Magic number** — every file begins with the ASCII bytes `wOF2` (`774f4632`). No HTML
  error page or redirect body slipped in.
- **`ccmp` / `mark` / `mkmk` retained** — every file carries `GSUB`, `GPOS` and `GDEF`.
  These are the tables that position stacked Vietnamese diacritics; without them marks sit at
  default offsets and collide with the base glyph. Google's slices keep them.
- **Newsreader is genuinely variable** — all six Newsreader files carry `fvar`, `gvar`, `avar`
  and `STAT`, i.e. the real `opsz 6..72` + `wght 200..800` axes, not a static instance.

Re-run `bash tools/subset-fonts.sh` to reproduce all three checks.

## 3. The three `unicode-range` values, verbatim

All six faces returned **byte-identical** `unicode-range` strings for a given subset, so there
are exactly three distinct values. Copy them exactly — do not reformat, reorder or "tidy" them.

**L — latin**

```
U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6, U+02DA, U+02DC, U+0304, U+0308, U+0329, U+2000-206F, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2191, U+2193, U+2212, U+2215, U+FEFF, U+FFFD
```

**LX — latin-ext**

```
U+0100-02BA, U+02BD-02C5, U+02C7-02CC, U+02CE-02D7, U+02DD-02FF, U+0304, U+0308, U+0329, U+1D00-1DBF, U+1E00-1E9F, U+1EF2-1EFF, U+2020, U+20A0-20AB, U+20AD-20C0, U+2113, U+2C60-2C7F, U+A720-A7FF
```

**VN — vietnamese**

```
U+0102-0103, U+0110-0111, U+0128-0129, U+0168-0169, U+01A0-01A1, U+01AF-01B0, U+0300-0301, U+0303-0304, U+0308-0309, U+0323, U+0329, U+1EA0-1EF9, U+20AB
```

The **VN** slice is the important one: it carries `Ă Đ Ĩ Ũ Ơ Ư`, the entire precomposed
`U+1EA0–U+1EF9` block (`ế ộ ữ ệ ậ …`) and `₫` (U+20AB). Vietnamese body copy mixes ASCII and
these codepoints in the same word, so a Vietnamese page fetches **latin *and* vietnamese** for
every face it renders. That is expected, not a bug.

## 5. Preload — 2 files per surface, and mind the depth

Fonts are **always** fetched in CORS mode, so `crossorigin` is required on the preload even
though these are same-origin. Omitting it causes a double download.

`href` is relative to the **HTML document**, so the prefix differs by directory depth:

| Page location | Prefix |
|---|---|
| `index.html`, `404.html` | `fonts/` |
| `blog/*.html` | `../fonts/` |
| `wy/*.html` | `../fonts/` |
| `test_html/vc.html` | `../fonts/` |

The spec's "preload exactly two faces per surface" budget now has to be read as **two files**.
Because Vietnamese text mixes ASCII and `U+1EA0–U+1EF9` inside a single word, the two files
that actually block first paint are the `latin` **and** `vietnamese` slices of the one face the
LCP text is set in — not two different families. Recommended:

```html
<!-- Surface A (index.html) — LCP is the Anton hero name, 27,292 B total -->
<link rel="preload" href="fonts/anton-400-latin.woff2"      as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="fonts/anton-400-vietnamese.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
```

```html
<!-- Surface B (blog/*.html) — LCP is Newsreader article body, 159,248 B total -->
<link rel="preload" href="../fonts/newsreader-vf-latin.woff2"      as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="../fonts/newsreader-vf-vietnamese.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
```

```html
<!-- Surface C (wy/*.html) — LCP is the Anton wordmark, 27,292 B total -->
<link rel="preload" href="../fonts/anton-400-latin.woff2"      as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="../fonts/anton-400-vietnamese.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
```

Everything else arrives via `font-display: swap`. Do not add a third preload — it competes with
the hero image and makes LCP worse.

**Surface B caveat:** preloading `newsreader-vf-latin.woff2` commits 132 KB before anything
else renders. If the article LCP element turns out to be a heading rather than body text,
preload the Be Vietnam Pro pair instead and let Newsreader swap in. Measure before committing.

## 6. Known cost: the `opsz` axis is 279 KB of the 700 KB

Measured against the Google Fonts API on 2026-07-26:

| Newsreader request | latin | latin-ext | vietnamese |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `opsz,wght@6..72,200..800` — **shipped** | 132,000 | 86,608 | 27,248 |
| `opsz,wght@6..72,400..700` — narrower weights | 132,000 | 86,608 | 27,248 |
| `wght@200..800` — **no `opsz` axis** | 58,084 | 36,244 | 11,932 |
| `wght@400;600` — "static" instances | 58,084 | 36,244 | 11,932 |

Two findings:

1. **Narrowing the weight range saves nothing.** Google serves identical bytes for
   `200..800` and `400..700`; the declared range is clamped in CSS only. There is no reason
   to ask for less than the full `200..800`.
2. **Dropping `opsz` would save 279,192 bytes** (~273 KiB, 39% of this directory) across the
   six Newsreader files. Requesting static instances is *not* a third option — Google returns
   the same weight-only variable file either way.

`opsz` was **kept** because it is load-bearing in the design system, not decorative:
`reports/design-style.md` specifies `font-optical-sizing: auto` globally, article body at
`opsz 16` and pull quotes at `opsz 48`, and `BRIEF.md` §6 T02 requires `opsz 6:72, wght 200:800`
explicitly. Dropping it is a design decision, not a build decision.

Note that `BRIEF.md` §2's estimate of "~62 KB" for `newsreader-vf-vn` matches the **no-`opsz`**
figure almost exactly (58 KB), so the brief's byte budget and the brief's feature requirement
were never consistent with each other. Flagging rather than silently picking one.

**If the owner decides 273 KB is not worth optical sizing**, the change is one line in
`tools/subset-fonts.sh` — drop `opsz,` and `6..72,` from `CSS_URL` — plus removing
`font-optical-sizing` from `css/base.css`. Filenames and `unicode-range` values do not change.

---

## 7. Not included, deliberately

- **Poppins.** It has no `vietnamese` subset — `latin-ext` covers `ă ơ ư đ` but every
  tone-marked vowel lives in `U+1EA0–U+1EF9`, which Poppins does not contain. This is the
  live bug that makes `Hướng dẫn học` font-switch mid-word on the current site
  (`BRIEF.md` R11, `design-style.md` §3.2). Every role it held moves to Be Vietnam Pro.
- **Cyrillic / Greek subsets.** None of these three families offer them. The filter in
  `tools/subset-fonts.sh` drops them anyway if a future version adds them.
- **Font Awesome.** The site currently loads 5.15.3 *and* 6.0.0-beta3 (~75 KB of duplicate
  icon CSS on every page). Both `<link>`s are replaced by `img/sprite.svg` (T05).

## 8. Licensing

All three families are licensed under the **SIL Open Font License 1.1**, which permits
self-hosting and redistribution. Anton and Newsreader are by Vernon Adams / Production Type
respectively; Be Vietnam Pro is by Bien Studio. The OFL requires the license travel with the
fonts — if the full OFL text is ever needed, it is at
`https://openfontlicense.org/open-font-license-official-text/`.

## 9. Regenerating

```bash
bash tools/subset-fonts.sh --dry-run   # show the plan, download nothing
bash tools/subset-fonts.sh             # download, verify wOF2, dump sfnt tables
```

Google revs the version segment in the `fonts.gstatic.com` path (`/v27/`, `/v12/`, `/v26/`
as of this capture) when a family is updated, so re-running may legitimately change the bytes.
**Update the table in §2 if it does.** Nothing here runs at deploy time — the `.woff2` files
are committed artefacts and GitHub Pages uploads the repo root verbatim.
